title: Credential flow microcards and code strip for API/SDK quickstart
creator: Sofia Ramirez
description: Design a compact, modular set of visual assets to be used across the API/SDK quickstart docs that concisely explain credentials (create, rotate, revoke), streaming behavior, and tool-calling examples. Assets should be optimized for in-doc inline usage and for the product release notes: microcards (3-step visual tiles), a horizontal code-strip component for SDK snippets, annotated screenshots of Console and Quickstart modals, and small animated GIFs illustrating streaming/token streaming and tool call lifecycle.
objectives: Make the credential flow teachable in three quick visual steps
Provide a reusable code-strip component for single-line SDK examples
Show streaming as incremental tokens without overwhelming the user
Create assets that match Redwood design system tokens and are accessible
deliverables: Code-strip component: SVG + CSS token examples
4 annotated product screenshots (Console keys, Quickstart modal, Streaming demo, Tool call structured output)
2 small GIFs demonstrating streaming partials and a tool call round-trip
Figma source file with component library and export presets
Copy snippets for each asset and alt-text for accessibility
tasks: Design microcard template and layout (3-step flow) - Sofia
Create code-strip component with copy-to-clipboard affordance - Aisha
Capture annotated screenshots from staging Console - Engineering ops
Produce GIFs using headless recording and GIF optimization - Design
Handoff Figma components + export tokens to docs writers
Review with PM and API team; iterate on copy and security phrasing
acceptance_criteria: Microcards communicate credential lifecycle in <= 3 short captions
Code-strip component renders correctly at 320px and 1280px widths
All assets exported in PNG/SVG and meet 4.5:1 contrast for text
Screenshots align with Console UI v2026-03 and include redaction where needed
GIFs remain under 1MB each after optimization
Design files and export instructions committed to Figma and linked in ticket
review_feedback: PM (Marco Nguyen): simplify copy for non-technical product managers; remove jargon in step 2
Eng (Ethan Chung): prefer showing key partial redaction in Console screenshot; confirm rotation API path
Security (Leila Osei): call out 'do not commit keys' in microcard caption and add small security badge
Docs (Anika Bose): request alternate code-strip with 'curl' + 'node' tabs
decisions: Use three microcard steps: Generate -> Use (SDK snippet) -> Rotate/Disable
Code-strip will be monospace SVG with selectable text and explicit copy button
Streaming GIF will show token-level progressive reveal rather than a loader bar to illustrate partial outputs
Dark-mode variants required due to docs dark theme launch
tradeoffs: Including full SDK snippet increases real-estate; we will use a shortened inline snippet with a link to a full example
GIF size vs clarity: optimize to keep under 1MB at expense of some frame rate
Redaction in screenshots reduces fidelity for QA but necessary for security
